The present petition filed under Section 482 of the CrPC seeks quashing of the Fir No.
1144/2022, under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Ipc, registered at P.S. Aman Vihar.
2.

The marriage between petitioner no.1/husband and respondent no.2/wife was solemnized on 21.06.2020 as per Muslim rites and ceremonies.
3. No child was born out of the said wedlock.
4. Due to matrimonial differences between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2, the parties started residing separately since 10.04.2021.

5.

On 14.07.2023, parties arrived at a settlement before the Mediation Centre, Rohini District Courts, Delhi and as per the said settlement deed, petitioner no.1 has agreed to pay an amount of Rs.
5,60,000/- to the respondent no.2/wife towards full and final settlement of all her claims including istridhan, permanent alimony and maintenance - present, past and future including mehar.

The copy of the aforesaid settlement deed dated 14.07.2023 is on record (Annexure P-3).
6.
The marriage between the parties stands dissolved as per the Muslim Law/Shariyat Law on 06.04.2023.

Further, as per the settlement deed, an amount of Rs. 2,60,000/- has already been paid to respondent no.2 and the remaining amount of Rs. 3,00,000/- has been paid to her in court today,
by means of a demand draft.

7. Petitioners and complainant/respondent no. 2 are present before the Court and have been duly identified by their respective counsel, as well as the Investigating Officer, ASI Sanjeev, PS Aman Vihar.

8. A demand draft bearing no. 263481 dated 30.08.2023 for Rs. 3,00,000/- drawn on UCO Bank,
Delhi High Court (DHC) branch, has been handed over complainant/respondent no.2, who acknowledges the receipt of the same.
9. The complainant/respondent no.2 states that the matter has been settled with the petitioners and she has no objection if the FIR is quashed.
She further states that all the terms of the agreement have been complied with.

sentences.text: 12. In view of the aforesaid circumstances, and the fact that the parties have put a quietus to the dispute, no useful purpose will be served in continuing with the present FIR No. 1144/2022, under Sections 498A/406/34 of the IPC, registered at P.S. Aman Vihar.
13. In the interest of justice, the petition is allowed, and the FIR No. 1144/2022, under Sections 498A/406/34 of the IPC, registered at P.S. Aman Vihar, Delhi, is hereby quashed.
14. Petition is allowed and disposed of accordingly.
15. Pending application(s), if any, also stand disposed of.
